row.body: Two keys are taped to separate collection times. A bottle marked for the passenger has no return mark, though the driver’s sheet says every seat was cleared.
row.title: The unfinished handoff

sidecar.gloss: A passenger’s bottle is left behind despite a completed seat record.
sidecar.rival_reading: A household move or field visit could explain the keys and bottle; the completed seat sheet does not prove an evacuation failed.

row.body: opposite route arrows are painted on the paperclip box and hand radio. the older arrow was scraped away beneath fresh road grit.
row.title: missing count beside the paperclip box

sidecar.gloss: A response bundle preserves a missing count, changed route, or erased identity.
sidecar.rival_reading: A farm-program crew could have counted routes, repacked tools, or removed ownership marks during hurried field work; the objects do not prove a concealed public response.

row.body: The room smells like the liquid from the field bottles, and Mom’s throat still hurts. I opened the window; the return truck says nothing spilled.
row.title: Kept from the drawer

sidecar.gloss: A family member links a lingering illness to a field bottle smell, while a return note denies a spill.
sidecar.rival_reading: A cleanup crew may have used disinfectant after an emergency; the letter does not establish what liquid caused the irritation.
